knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper proposes a method combining recurrent neural networks with diffusion models for probabilistic time series forecasting. It addresses scalability issues in generative models by extending stochastic interpolants to a conditional generation framework. The approach aims to capture complex high-dimensional distributions and cross-feature dependencies more efficiently than standard autoregressive or pure generative models.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The proposed generative model learns the joint density of a time series window comprising context and prediction segments, addressing scalability issues inherent in models where size depends on window length. By leveraging the strong correlation between neighboring time points, the method initiates prediction from the current time point to improve sample quality and reduce inference complexity. The framework combines the computational efficiency of recurrent neural networks for encoding temporal history with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of diffusion models.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The stochastic interpolant framework models velocity and score functions using deep neural networks trained via mean squared error loss. Inference utilizes forward and backward stochastic differential equations (SDEs) to generate samples from conditional or joint densities. The method supports conditional generation by incorporating additional features into the velocity and score functions.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The proposed method uses a recurrent neural network to encode context into a history prompt, enabling stochastic interpolants to perform conditional generation for time series prediction. Importance sampling with a Beta distribution is employed to stabilize training by addressing high loss values near the boundaries of the diffusion time. The approach supports recursive multi-step prediction and is evaluated on synthetic and real-world datasets.

attributes.purpose: Stabilize training by handling integral over diffusion time

relationships.target: larger loss values when s is close to two ends

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study compares stochastic interpolants (SI) with diffusion and flow-based models on synthetic and real-world time series datasets. SI demonstrates competitive performance in multivariate probabilistic forecasting, outperforming or matching baselines on most datasets. The method utilizes a recurrent neural network to encode context for conditional generation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluates a stochastic interpolant-based model on four real-world time series datasets using CRPS-sum, NRMSE, and ND metrics. The proposed method outperforms or matches baselines on three datasets, with Flow Matching performing better only on the Traffic dataset. The authors conclude that stochastic interpolants are a strong candidate for conditional generation in multivariate probabilistic forecasting.
